_README: FROZEN PRE-REGISTRATION for the prospective reward-repair experiment.
Everything below was fixed BEFORE the sealed evaluation split was generated
and before any arm was trained. Nothing here may be changed after the sealed
split is opened. If something must change, bump `revision`, record why in
`amendments`, and state in the paper that the change happened after freeze.
The point of this file is that a reader can check what we committed to
against what we report. It is the direct answer to the failure this paper
documents: a reward that looked fine by every metric we chose after seeing

amendments.summary: Operationalized already-declared logging, training, split generation, and analysis rules before any sealed design was generated or viewed.
detail: Revision 1 declared procedures that were not yet executable or not yet
numerically defined. No sealed design existed, none was viewed, and no
arm had been trained when this revision was written, so nothing here is
informed by an outcome. Specifically:
(a) grpo_oracle.py did not implement the rf_struct reward, did not log
flat groups or raw candidates, and checkpointed by attempted step
rather than by optimizer update. Implemented, then re-hashed.
(b) gen_accelerator_catalog.py emits fixed grids and had no seed-driven
selection, so seed 20260813 alone did not determine the split. A
dedicated generator (gen_sealed_split.py) now does, and is hashed
before being run.
(c) 'substantial part of the original gain' and 'late divergence' had no
numerical definitions. Both now do.
(d) The all-or-nothing conjunctive success criterion was replaced by an
exhaustive outcome taxonomy, so a partial result has a predefined
name instead of being classified after the fact.
(e) Identities were pinned at 16 hex characters for scripts only; the
model, adapter, reward artifact and labelled rows were unpinned.
Full SHA-256 for all of them, with the hash basis stated.
(f) canonicalize.py gained a compiles() helper used by the reward-time
gate. This is ADDITIVE: canonicalisation behaviour is unchanged and
the version stays 1.6.1, but the file hash changed, so the byte
contract and Check A are re-run at the new hash to confirm the
reported results still hold. If either differs, this revision is
void and the difference is reported.

amendments.type: pre-outcome correction, from an existing log; no sealed data consulted
amendments.summary: The attempt ceiling is PER ARM, not shared: 2000 for rf_struct and mlp, 4500 for correctness-only.
detail: Revision 2 set one shared ceiling of 2000 attempted groups. That silently
reintroduces step-matching, which the protocol explicitly rejects, because a
flat group produces no gradient and the flat RATE differs by arm by
construction.
Measured on grpo_ablate_const_matched_log.jsonl, which predates this
experiment: the binary-correctness reward went non-flat on 159 of 1997 groups
(0.080). The cause is structural, not a defect -- a group is flat when all 8
candidates are correct OR all 8 are wrong, and sft_v6c is ~95% correct on
train designs, so 0.95^8 = 0.66 of groups are unanimously correct. Reaching
276 non-flat updates therefore needs ~3450 attempted groups.
Under the shared ceiling the correctness arm would have stopped near 160
updates against 276 for the others, so the one arm designed to REMOVE a
confound would have acquired one.
The matched quantity is unchanged: 276 non-flat optimizer updates for every
arm. Only the number of attempts differs, which is what matching on updates
means. Ceilings: rf_struct 2000, mlp 2000 (both need ~440), correctness 4500
Consequence for the budget cut order: two ceiling-capped correctness arms
would cost MORE wall clock than one full-budget arm (2 x 2000 = 4000 groups
versus 3450) while being confounded, so the correctness arm runs at full
budget with ONE seed. The prospective correctness result is labelled
single-seed. This reverses part of the external reviewer's cut order, which
assumed all arms cost the same per update.

amendments.type: pre-outcome executability and fail-closed analysis amendment
amendments.summary: Added the missing sealed evaluator and actual-candidate gate, replaced manual or permissive analysis inputs with artifact-derived checks, and made hash verification cover every required dependency.
detail: No sealed-policy evaluation artifact or completed study arm is present in
the repository, and no sealed outcome was consulted while making this
amendment. A direct read-only server audit was attempted on 2026-08-18 but
the SSH endpoint closed the connection; run_arm.sh therefore additionally
refuses any pre-existing arm output before a server launch.
Revision 2 named eval_holdout.py, but that script can evaluate only the old
30-design split and cannot consume sealed_split.json. eval_sealed.py now
loads the frozen prompts and per-design token budgets directly, uses the
fixed generation and oracle seeds, emits only distinct oracle-correct RTL,
and preserves total sample counts even when a design has zero correct RTL.
Revision 2 required a pre-open mutation/trace contract over the actual RF
training candidates but supplied no way to construct that corpus.
materialize_rf_candidates.py now deterministically extracts every distinct
non-empty RTL candidate from both complete RF group logs, with source-row
and content-hash provenance, before canonicalize.py --check-traces runs.
The frozen revision-2 analyzer could silently omit zero-correct designs,
accepted missing or partial synthesis inputs, accepted manually entered
reward-resolution and gate values, did not enforce training completion, and
encoded the pre-amendment correctness-arm seed count. analyze_sealed_v3.py
fails on those cases and derives diagnostics from manifests, PPA rows, both
RF group logs, and the mutation-contract artifact.
The correctness-only arm has one training seed under amendment 1 but retains
the frozen 48-draw per-arm evaluation budget. Two-seed arms use 24 draws per
training seed. If the sole permitted MLP seed-2 budget cut is exercised, its
remaining seed receives 48 draws. The RF midpoint remains 8 draws per seed.
Generation batching is fixed at four for all sealed evaluations. It affects
the deterministic random-number consumption pattern but not an endpoint or
threshold, and is set before any sealed generation.
verify_sealed_training.py requires all five declared runs, exact configs,
updates 1 through 276, and checkpoints 138 and 276 before sealed generation.
verify_sealed_ppa.py requires one explicit PPA row for every manifest
candidate; an interrupted or partial Vivado batch cannot be scored as failure.
run_arm.sh now rejects non-declared arm/seed pairs and every stale output.
freeze_hashes.py previously verified only keys already present in hashes.json,
so a newly required script could be silently unpinned. Verification now also
fails on every required-but-unpinned or unresolved artifact. All revision-3
workflow scripts and their regression tests are added to the identity set.
No scientific endpoint, threshold, split member, reward model, training
hyperparameter, synthesis target, bootstrap rule, or outcome label changed.

amendments.summary: Disclosed and retained one complete revision-2 RF training seed discovered after server access was restored; archived every incomplete run and fixed the balanced hardware allocation for the remaining four jobs.
detail: Revision 3 truthfully reported that no completed arm was present in the
committed repository and that the server audit endpoint was inaccessible.
When access to two replacement container ports was supplied on 2026-08-19,
the shared untracked server state was found to contain one complete
rf_struct seed-1 run and three incomplete processes (rf_struct seed 2,
MLP seed 1, and correctness seed 1). No sealed-policy evaluation directory
or sealed outcome was opened, generated, or inspected before this amendment.
The complete rf_struct seed-1 run ended at exactly 276 non-flat updates,
contains checkpoints 138 and 276, and its launch-time revision-2 hash
manifest verifies 27 pinned artifacts with zero changes and zero missing.
Its run_config records the frozen seed, group size, token budget, learning
rate, KL coefficient, reward, attempt ceiling, checkpoint schedule, model,
adapter, and code hashes. The training implementation, oracle, candidate
catalogue, SFT corpus logic, RF reward artifact, SFT adapter, and base model
are byte-identical between launch commit 3110c88 and revision 4. Revision 3
changed fail-closed launch, evaluation, PPA, and analysis auditing rather
than the optimizer computation that produced this completed checkpoint.
The complete rf_struct seed-1 run is therefore retained prospectively and
its launch hashes, preregistration, and run_arm.sh are copied beside it.
The three interrupted runs were terminated and moved, with their logs and
partial adapters, to abandoned_runs/pre_rev3_stopped_20260819. They are not
resumed, merged, or analysed; each is rerun from update zero as originally
specified by the crash policy.
The remaining jobs are balanced across the two available GPU types before
launch: rf_struct seed 2 and MLP seed 2 on the V100S-PCIe box; MLP seed 1
and the single-seed correctness control on the V100-SXM2 box. Thus each
two-seed reward arm spans both boxes rather than confounding arm with box.
No endpoint, threshold, split member, reward, model, optimizer setting,
sample count, synthesis flow, bootstrap rule, or outcome label changed.

amendments.summary: Relocated the incomplete correctness control from a V100-SXM2 to one L40S GPU after an isolated, version-matched environment and content-identical model copy passed inference and optimizer-update canaries; fixed FP16 explicitly for every arm.
detail: No sealed split was opened for policy evaluation, no sealed candidate was
generated or synthesised, and no efficacy outcome was available or consulted
before this amendment. Active-run attempted-group and update counts were
viewed only to estimate completion time; the partial correctness run is
discarded under the existing crash/restart rule and contributes no result.
The L40S host is restricted to /home/adam/mas/mas. A new isolated environment
there uses Python 3.10.20, torch 2.4.1+cu121, transformers 4.46.3, PEFT
0.13.2, accelerate 1.0.1, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3, scikit-learn 1.7.2,
joblib 1.5.3, and Icarus Verilog 12.0, with PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 and every
environment, cache, temporary, model, repository, and output path kept under
that permitted directory.
The copied base model and SFT adapter have the same full manifest digests as
the frozen server objects. All other required artifacts match the frozen
identity set, and both the functional-oracle canary and hash verification pass.
Two non-study operational canaries used undeclared seeds 999 and 998 solely
to test inference and one complete backward/optimizer/checkpoint path. They
are never treated as study arms, efficacy evidence, or selectable results.
Because automatic dtype selection would choose BF16 on L40S but FP16 on V100,
run_arm.sh now passes --dtype fp16 explicitly and the completion audit rejects
any other dtype. The already completed RF seed 1 and every active V100 job
record FP16, so this prevents hardware from changing training precision.
run_arm.sh also accepts the prospectively allocated physical GPU 4 and an
explicit environment-bin path. The correctness seed-1 arm restarts from update
zero on that GPU with the same seed, model, adapter, prompts, reward, optimizer,
hyperparameters, update target, attempt ceiling, checkpoints, and crash policy.
No endpoint, threshold, split member, reward, model content, optimizer setting,
sample count, synthesis flow, bootstrap rule, or outcome label changed. The
relocation changes only host hardware and wall-clock time.

_backend_rationale: The yosys backend reached 33/60 on the byte contract and would ALSO need
an RTLIL-specific feature extractor, because the features below count
Verilog tokens that `proc; opt_clean` no longer represents. It is future
work. The claim we make is LEXICAL invariance, not canonical hardware
canonicaliser._suite_note: `reflow` is the attack the policy actually used (one statement per line) and `pack` is its inverse, so the exploited channel is in the suite by construction.

trace_audit._note: sampled full-trace equality on 256 vectors under two seeds. NOT exhaustive over the input space.

evidence_limits: Token-level self-checks cannot generally certify source preservation.
Compilation detects syntactic corruption; sampled full-trace equality
supplies stronger semantic evidence, though not formal equivalence.
Concretely: two tokenizer defects ('0 -> ' 0 and $signed -> $ signed)
passed the entire byte-level contract -- idempotence, metamorphic equality
across all six mutations, feature equality -- while emitting invalid
Verilog, because a consistently broken output is still self-consistent. A
token-count guard was built for this class and provably does not fire ('0
is two tokens and ' 0 re-tokenises to the same two), so it is retained
only for the narrower 'a construct vanished' case. But compilation is not
sufficient either: a canonicaliser can emit valid Verilog that behaves
differently -- a rename that merged two signals would compile cleanly.
That is why trace equality is run over the whole corpus and why neither
mandatory_recheck: --check-traces over the FULL corpus is mandatory and must be re-run
whenever the corpus, the canonicaliser or the tokenizer changes.
Additionally, before the sealed split is opened, the mutation contract is
re-run over every DISTINCT candidate produced by the rf_struct arm during
training. If any new failure appears, the experiment is classified
invalid_repair under the existing stop rule and reported as such. It is

hardware meaning. nb_assign replaced: it was line-anchored. accum
replaced: it matched a signal-NAME regex. n_loops / loop_bound_* ADDED
after Check A failed on the median family, on TRAINING data only, before

measured 60.4 and 38.3 MHz with identical feature vectors. A loop bound
determines the synthesised hardware and no layout change can alter it.
The representation was moved; the thresholds were not.

2. the canonicaliser must accept it -- Unsupported => reward 0, logged;
3. the canonical form must COMPILE -- invalid => reward 0, logged.

reason, so the rate of each is a reportable number rather than an

check_a._purpose: does canonicalisation destroy the information needed to ORDER candidates?
check_a._med_caveat: med at 21.7% (5 unorderable of 23 material pairs) is a MARGINAL pass against a 25% ceiling that was fixed before the run. Report it as marginal; never quote 1.3% alone.
med_decision: med is RETAINED. Excluding the known-hard family after seeing this
diagnostic would weaken the experiment and invite a more serious
objection. It is predeclared a HIGH-RISK STRATUM: reported separately in
every table, and carried at equal weight in the primary aggregate. It is
not removed or downweighted later whatever it shows.

check_b._name: reward-resolution failure (a diagnosed null, not an expected outcome)
check_b.eligible_group: >= 2 oracle-correct candidates with distinct canonical feature vectors
check_b.resolved_group: rf_struct prediction range over the group > 5 MHz
check_b.plateau_diagnosed_if: < 20% of eligible groups resolved over the fixed run
check_b.measured_from: the per-candidate group log, directly (not reconstructed)

sealed_split.generator: gen_sealed_split.py, hashed before it is run
sealed_split.layout: 2 per family per regime, before the replacement rule below

regime_definition.interpolation: parameters INSIDE the trained range (fir/firr taps 4..32, poly degree 2..10, iir order 2..14, med W 3..9)
regime_definition.extrapolation: parameters OUTSIDE it, excluding the §5 held-out values

coefficient_axis: The trained grid covers EVERY fir/firr tap count in 4..32, so an unseen
tap count inside the trained range does not exist. A new coefficient set
at a trained tap count IS an unseen design -- different constant
multipliers, different synthesised hardware, different Fmax -- lying
inside the trained region, which is what interpolation means. poly and
iir already had this axis; fir/firr gain fir_coeffs_var/firr_coeffs_var.
firr variants stay affine in the tap index (a*(k+1)+b) so the family keeps
its defining property of having no coefficient table.
replacement_rule: med's interpolation pool is PROVABLY EMPTY: a median filter is defined by
its window width alone, there is no coefficient to vary, and every width
inside the trained range is consumed by the train grid {3,5,9} or the §5
held-out set {7,11}. Its two interpolation slots are reallocated to the
following families in the fixed order (fir, firr, poly, iir, med), one at
a time, giving interp = fir 3, firr 3, poly 2, iir 2, med 0 and extrap =
2 each. The total stays 20 and each regime keeps 10 designs. med still
supplies both extrapolation designs, so all five families appear.
eligibility: A design is ELIGIBLE if AT LEAST ONE of its correct styles satisfies every
gate; styles are tried shortest-first and the witness style is recorded.
Gates are properties of the DESIGN, never of an outcome: (a) the oracle can
build a reference for the name; (b) the style fits the family's generation
budget; (c) the style passes the oracle; (d) the canonicaliser accepts it
and the canonical form is trace-equal.
(b) is the F4 truncation failure as a rule: a design whose every correct
form overflows the budget is unanswerable by construction and would measure
the budget rather than the policy. (d) prevents a design on which the
rf_struct arm would be structurally blind.
The any-style form matters and was not hypothetical: validating against one
arbitrary style rejected the ENTIRE median extrapolation pool, because
med_comb is a fully unrolled comparator network needing 6670 tokens at W=13
while med_sort expresses the same filter in about 680. The designs were
always answerable; the witness was wrong. This was found and fixed before
Rejections are recorded with reasons in sealed_split.json.
sealed_split._budget_note: med11 already exceeded 1536 (F4), so every sealed med design is generated at 3072. Pinned here so evaluation cannot quietly choose another budget.
sealed_split.isolation_mechanism: gen_sft_corpus.is_holdout() returns True for every design in sealed_split.json and for every fir/firr coefficient-variant name form, so isolation does not depend on the manifest file being present
sealed_split.open_condition: after every preregistered training seed for all arms is complete, every configuration is frozen, freeze_hashes.py --verify passes, verify_sealed_training.py passes, and the pre-open mutation contract over the rf_struct arm's actual training candidates has passed
sealed_split._honest_limitation: These are unseen PARAMETERISATIONS from the same generator families, restricted to designs whose reference is canonicalisable and fits the generation budget. That repairs adaptive reuse of the old 30-design set. It does NOT establish cross-template generalisation, and the paper must say so. External circuits are a TCAD extension.

arms.name: sft
arms._note: evaluation-only non-RL baseline, 48 samples per design

arms.name: grpo_correctness_only
arms._seed_note: single seed: full budget beats two ceiling-capped seeds on both cost and validity (amendment 1)

budget_cut_order: If six runs cannot be afforded, the cut is grpo_mlp_original seed 2, and
only that. The correctness-only arm answers the critical causal objection --
whether improvement comes from the physical reward or merely from
correctness pressure plus SFT style bias -- and cannot be inferred from
history. The original MLP already has a measured v8 trajectory showing both
genuine early gains and later exploitation. If it runs single-seed, the
prospective MLP result is LABELLED single-seed and the historical v8 result
is cited as supporting, not independent, evidence.

training_protocol.matched_on: non-flat optimizer updates, NOT attempted steps
training_protocol._target_rationale: matches the v8 trajectory the diagnosis is based on (step 400 = 276 non-flat updates)
training_protocol._ceiling_rationale: a run that reaches the attempt ceiling before the target ends there and is REPORTED as having ended on the ceiling; it is never silently extended
training_protocol._checkpoint_note: indexed by optimizer update, not attempted step: arms are matched on updates, so a step-indexed checkpoint compares different amounts of learning across arms. A target never reached means that checkpoint does not exist; a nearby checkpoint is never substituted.
training_protocol.kl_reference: frozen copy of the SFT adapter (F3), not the base model
training_protocol.design_and_prompt_manifest: written to <out>/run_config.json at run start (designs list + all hyperparameters + code hashes + GPU + dtype)
crash_restart_policy: A run that crashes is DISCARDED and restarted from step 0 with the same
seed. Partial runs are never resumed and never merged. grpo_oracle.py
refuses to start if a non-empty group log already exists at the target
path, so this is enforced rather than intended.
training_protocol._logging_rationale: The invariance gate's operational columns were computed over RECONSTRUCTED (policy, design) sets of deduplicated evaluation candidates, not the actual 8-sample training groups. They are counterfactual decision-sensitivity metrics. This logging makes the prospective numbers direct measurements instead. Canonical features are logged for EVERY arm, including those whose reward never reads them, because the exploit is only visible by comparing line-anchored against layout-blind features.

evaluation._mid_note: 8 samples/design/seed at update 138 for the rf_struct arm only, generated BEFORE opening and synthesised in the same one-time batch, so late divergence is measurable at more than one checkpoint. If this batch is not affordable, 'late divergence' is dropped and replaced by the weaker measurable statement 'no endpoint reward-reality sign disagreement', and the paper says which was used.

generation_seeds._note: generation RNG seeds, distinct from training seeds and from oracle stimulus seeds

evaluation._synthesis_caveat: WNS-derived from a single implementation run. NOT timing closure. All comparisons relative, identical flow.
evaluation.duplicate_handling: synthesised once, but weighted by multiplicity in the sample-weighted endpoints; deduplicating would silently reward a policy that concentrates on one output, and that concentration is a real property
evaluation.failure_handling: incorrect, oracle-error, synthesis-failure and timeout all score ZERO in the equal-sample endpoint
evaluation.design_aggregation: unweighted mean over designs; design is the unit of independence
evaluation.primary_endpoint: mean over designs of (arm - SFT) equal-sample Fmax, where equal-sample Fmax = sum(multiplicity x real Fmax) / total samples drawn, with failures scored zero

uncertainty.pairing: identical resampled design indices applied to every arm
uncertainty.seed_handling: the two training seeds are averaged within design for the combined interval, and each seed is ALSO reported separately; they are never pooled as independent samples

evaluation.analysis_script: analyze_sealed_v3.py under the revision-3 pre-outcome amendment; the revision-2 analyze_sealed.py is retained and hashed as historical evidence

power._note: planning estimate from the committed v8 design differences, recorded so the resolvable effect size is not decided after the fact
power.adequate_for: effects resembling the prior 77-119 MHz gains
power.family_claims: two designs per family x regime do not support inferential family-specific claims; family results are DESCRIPTIVE only

outcome_taxonomy._note: Exact invariance is a VALIDITY GATE, not an efficacy criterion. Exactly one label is assigned by analyze_sealed_v3.py from the frozen rules below. 'Retains at least 50% of the prospective original-MLP improvement on the same sealed designs' is a HIGH-RETENTION MODIFIER on a successful outcome, not part of the success gate -- otherwise an unexpected failure of the original MLP on the new split would make the repaired reward impossible to classify. If the MLP improvement is non-positive, retention is NOT APPLICABLE.

labels.name: invalid_repair
labels.definition: prospective exact-invariance, canonical-compilation, or semantic gate fails

labels.name: full_two_regime_repair
labels.definition: valid; rf_struct beats SFT in both seeds and both regimes; seed-averaged 95% CIs exclude zero; no late divergence

labels.name: directional_but_imprecise
labels.definition: both seeds improve in a regime, but its CI includes zero

labels.name: regime_limited
labels.definition: stable improvement in exactly one regime

labels.name: reward_resolution_failure
labels.definition: fewer than 20% of eligible training groups are resolved

labels.name: reward_misalignment
labels.definition: reward/policy moves, but real Fmax does not improve or diverges

labels.name: stable_null
labels.definition: valid, resolved reward and no divergence, but negligible real improvement

late_divergence.definition: reward increases materially from update 138 to update 276 while equal-sample real Fmax decreases materially in the same regime
late_divergence.requires: the mid-checkpoint evaluation; without it the weaker 'no endpoint reward-reality sign disagreement' is the most that may be claimed

high_retention.denominator: prospective original-MLP improvement on the same sealed designs

stop_rules: One canonicaliser version after this freeze.
NO tuning after the sealed results are opened.
If a different structural exploit appears: report the boundary, do not build repair v2.
If the pre-open mutation contract over the rf_struct arm's training candidates fails: classify invalid_repair and report it; do not repair and re-run.
If seeds disagree: report seed_unstable, do not add seeds until significance appears.
No new corpora, boards, EDA tools, reward architectures or mutation families before submission.
